summary: How far apart two dates are, in a unit you choose. Signed, and unrounded for fixed units.
description: Date Difference answers To minus From, counted in the chosen unit. It is signed — positive when To is later — so 'days until' and 'days since' are the same node read two ways, and Absolute drops the sign when only the distance matters. Fixed units divide exactly and are NOT rounded: 36 hours is 1.5 days. Months and years are counted in whole calendar steps, because a fractional month is not a quantity anyone can check; the answer is how many whole steps Date Add could take without overshooting, so 31 January to 28 February is 1 month and 31 January to 27 February is 0.
whenToUse: Age, elapsed time, 'days remaining', SLA windows, deciding whether something is stale.

ports.from: The earlier instant, in the reading that makes Difference positive.
ports.to: The later instant. Difference is negative when this is actually earlier.
ports.unit: What Difference counts. Days by default.
ports.absolute: Drop the sign, so the output is a distance rather than a direction.
ports.difference: To minus From, in Unit. Unset while either date is missing or unreadable.
ports.changed: Fires after Difference has been recomputed.
ports.failure: Invalid Date — fires when a date arrived that could not be read.

patterns: Record date → From, Now Date → To, unit Days: how old this record is.
antiPatterns: Assuming the result is a whole number. Fixed units are deliberately fractional; round it downstream if you need to.
